question.text: Scenario: Arun Kumar is analyzing Reliance Industries (RIL) stock using multiple technical indicators. Current observations: (1) RIL CMP: Rs.2,850. (2) 50-day SMA: Rs.2,780 (rising). 200-day SMA: Rs.2,650 (rising). (3) The 50-day SMA crossed above the 200-day SMA one month ago. (4) RSI: 58. (5) Bollinger Bands: Upper band Rs.2,950, Middle band Rs.2,780, Lower band Rs.2,610. Price is between middle and upper band. (6) Strong support at Rs.2,600 (tested 3 times in last 6 months). (7) Resistance at Rs.2,950 (tested twice). (8) Volume has been above average on recent up-days. (9) MACD is above the signal line and above the zero baseline. Question 5 of 5: Based on all technical indicators, Arun's recommendation for RIL should be:

answer.text: Strong Sell because the stock is at Rs.2,850 — too high
Buy/Hold with a target near resistance at Rs.2,950 and a stop-loss just below support around Rs.2,600 — all indicators are bullish
Wait indefinitely for the stock to fall to Rs.2,000
Short sell immediately with no stop-loss

explanation.text: The Logic: The technical picture is uniformly bullish: a golden cross (50-day SMA above 200-day SMA) has occurred, price is above both rising moving averages, RSI of 58 is neutral with room to run, MACD is above its signal line and above the zero baseline, and volume is above average on up-days (a positive On-Balance Volume signal). With strong support around Rs.2,600 (tested 3 times) and resistance at Rs.2,950 (tested twice), the workbook guidance is to set the target near resistance (Rs.2,950) and place the stop-loss just below the support level (around Rs.2,600). The Trap: "Stock is too high" ignores trend analysis. Trading without a stop-loss is contrary to standard risk management. A stop-loss "near the 50-day SMA" is not the placement rule given in the source - the workbook places stops just below support (for longs) or just above resistance (for shorts). Note: Source - NISM-Series-XV Research Analyst workbook (February 2026), pp. 314 (stop-loss placement at support/resistance), 317-318 (MACD and moving-average synthesis), and 323 (OBV).
